phases.name: Foundations
phases.goal: Rebuild core DSA patterns, C# fundamentals, system design basics and SQL so every later topic has a solid base.

phases.name: Core Depth
phases.goal: Go deep on .NET internals, EF Core, ASP.NET Core, Angular essentials and the first classic system designs while DSA moves into trees, heaps and graphs.

phases.name: Advanced Stack
phases.goal: Master advanced Next.js and Angular, Redis, Elasticsearch, Kubernetes and dynamic programming while continuing weekly system designs.

phases.name: Architecture and Scale
phases.goal: Own senior-level architecture topics: clean architecture, CQRS/event sourcing, payments, CI/CD, IaC and observability, plus hard DSA patterns.

phases.name: Interview Simulation
phases.goal: Run full mock loops, patch weak spots, polish stories and arrive rested and confident on interview day.

weeks.title: Arrays, C# and Fundamentals
weeks.goal: Restart DSA with hashing, refresh C# and OOP, learn the system design interview framework and build a story inventory.

weeks.title: Sliding Window, Collections and Caching
weeks.goal: Learn two pointers/sliding window/stack, .NET collections and generics, caching strategies, React basics and indexing.

weeks.title: Binary Search, LINQ and Docker
weeks.goal: Cover binary search and linked lists, LINQ and delegates, Angular standalone components, load balancing and Docker basics.

weeks.title: Trees, Async and DB Scaling
weeks.goal: Start trees, master async/await and React hooks, learn database scaling and build multi-container setups.

weeks.title: Tries, GC and Message Queues
weeks.goal: Finish core tree problems with tries, understand .NET memory/GC, Angular DI, queues and transaction isolation.

weeks.title: Heaps, EF Core and URL Shortener
weeks.goal: Learn heaps and backtracking, EF Core deeply, Next.js App Router, Angular routing and design a URL shortener.

weeks.title: Graphs, ASP.NET Core and Rate Limiter
weeks.goal: Start graphs, master the ASP.NET Core pipeline, read query plans, design a rate limiter and learn RSC.

weeks.title: Auth, Consistency and Midpoint Mock
weeks.goal: Cover topological sort, auth, Angular forms, distributed consistency, leadership stories and a first timed mock.

weeks.title: Union-Find, Dapper and Chat
weeks.goal: Learn union-find and Dijkstra, Dapper/minimal APIs, Next.js rendering, RxJS, 1D DP and design a chat system.

weeks.title: DP, Redis and News Feed
weeks.goal: Continue DP and intervals, go deep on Redis and Next.js caching, SignalR/background services and design a news feed.

weeks.title: 2D DP, Polly and Kubernetes
weeks.goal: Start 2D DP, resilience with Polly, Angular change detection/signals, Kubernetes core and a notification system.

weeks.title: Testing, Elasticsearch and NgRx
weeks.goal: Finish DP, master .NET testing, Elasticsearch, NgRx, K8s config/probes and design typeahead search.

weeks.title: Clean Architecture and CQRS
weeks.goal: Learn greedy and bit manipulation, clean architecture with MediatR, CQRS/event sourcing, Next.js auth and Helm.

weeks.title: Performance, Payments and CI/CD
weeks.goal: Re-solve hard array problems, tune .NET performance, design payments, Angular SSR, GitHub Actions and DB tradeoffs.

weeks.title: Hard Patterns, Ticketing and Terraform
weeks.goal: Tackle hard heap/graph problems, streaming in Next.js, ticketing design, Terraform/AWS, MassTransit and Angular testing.

weeks.title: Observability and Deep Dives
weeks.goal: Run a second timed mock, add observability, design file storage, finish Next.js, advanced C# and resume defense.

weeks.title: Mock Designs and Re-solve Sprints
weeks.goal: Re-solve trees/graphs/DP, learn deployment strategies, mock ride-sharing design and run .NET and behavioral mocks.

weeks.title: Rapid-fire and Mock Designs
weeks.goal: Run a third timed mock, design video streaming and a job scheduler, and drill frontend and SQL rapid-fire questions.

weeks.title: Full Mock Loops
weeks.goal: Simulate complete interview loops across coding, design, behavioral and .NET, then patch weak spots.

weeks.title: Final Polish and Rest
weeks.goal: Final mocks, negotiation prep, cheat sheets, logistics and a full rest day before interviews.

days.title: Arrays and Hashing I
days.summary: Hash maps and sets give O(1) lookups and are the first tool to reach for when a brute force is O(n^2). Most Blind75 easy questions reduce to a frequency count or a seen-set.

tasks.text: Study hash map/set lookup cost and the frequency-count pattern (NeetCode Arrays and Hashing intro)
LeetCode 217 - Contains Duplicate (Easy)
LeetCode 1 - Two Sum (Easy)
LeetCode 242 - Valid Anagram (Easy)

resources: Two Sum hash map solution C#

days.title: C# Fundamentals and OOP Refresher
days.summary: Senior .NET interviews still open with value vs reference types, boxing and OOP/SOLID questions. Crisp answers here set the tone for the rest of the loop.

tasks.text: Review value vs reference types, struct vs class, boxing/unboxing, ref/out/in parameters
Revisit OOP pillars and SOLID with C# examples; interface vs abstract class tradeoffs
Build a console Parking Lot system in C# using SOLID interfaces and unit-testable classes
Write 10 flashcards: record vs class, sealed, static, virtual/override, new modifier, readonly struct

resources: C# value types vs reference types boxing

days.title: System Design Fundamentals
days.summary: System design rounds reward a structured approach: clarify requirements, estimate, sketch, then deep dive. Learn the building blocks (DNS, HTTP, scaling, latency numbers) so you can reason out loud.

tasks.text: Learn client-server model, DNS resolution, HTTP/HTTPS, TCP vs UDP basics
Learn vertical vs horizontal scaling, stateless services and latency numbers every engineer should know
Memorize the 4-step framework: requirements, estimation, high-level design, deep dive
Draw your current production architecture (services, SQL, Redis, RabbitMQ, ES) in Excalidraw

resources: system design interview framework step by step
latency numbers every programmer should know

days.title: Arrays and Hashing II
days.summary: Grouping, bucketing and prefix/suffix products are core Medium patterns. They teach you to trade memory for time and to spot O(n) solutions.

tasks.text: LeetCode 49 - Group Anagrams (Medium)
LeetCode 347 - Top K Frequent Elements (Medium) - solve with bucket sort
LeetCode 238 - Product of Array Except Self (Medium)
LeetCode 125 - Valid Palindrome (Easy) - intro to two pointers

resources: Top K frequent elements bucket sort
Product of array except self prefix suffix

days.title: SQL Joins and Window Functions
days.summary: Many backend loops include a live SQL question. Joins, GROUP BY/HAVING and window functions cover most of them.

tasks.text: Review inner/left/right/full/cross/self joins, GROUP BY and HAVING
LeetCode SQL 181 - Employees Earning More Than Their Managers and 176 - Second Highest Salary
Learn window functions: ROW_NUMBER, RANK, DENSE_RANK, LAG/LEAD, running totals
LeetCode SQL 185 - Department Top Three Salaries (Hard) using DENSE_RANK

days.title: Story Inventory and Resume Audit
days.summary: Senior interviews weigh ownership and impact as much as code. Building a story bank early lets you rehearse all 20 weeks instead of cramming.

tasks.text: Audit resume: rewrite each bullet as action + technology + measurable impact
List 8 stories: outbox rollout, team lead, incident, conflict, mentoring, failure, tradeoff, deadline
Write 2 full STAR stories: a technical decision and a team conflict
Research what senior means at European/remote companies (ownership, async writing, autonomy)

resources: senior software engineer resume bullet examples

days.title: Week 1 Review
days.summary: Active recall beats rereading. Re-solve without looking, then summarize what you learned in your own words.

tasks.text: Re-solve LeetCode 1, 49 and 238 blind with a 20-minute timer each
Summarize the system design framework and scaling basics in 5 bullets
Tell one STAR story out loud in under 2 minutes and record it

resources: how to review leetcode problems effectively

days.title: Two Pointers and Sliding Window
days.summary: Two pointers and sliding windows turn nested loops into O(n). Know fixed vs variable windows and when to shrink.

tasks.text: LeetCode 15 - 3Sum (Medium) - focus on skipping duplicates
LeetCode 11 - Container With Most Water (Medium)
LeetCode 121 - Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock (Easy)
LeetCode 3 - Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters (Medium)

days.title: .NET Collections and Generics
days.summary: Interviewers probe whether you know how List, Dictionary and HashSet work internally and which interface to expose. Generics, constraints and variance are classic senior questions.

tasks.text: Learn List/Dictionary/HashSet internals: resizing, hashing, collisions, GetHashCode/Equals contract
Compare IEnumerable vs ICollection vs IList vs IReadOnlyList vs IQueryable
Learn generic constraints, covariance (out) and contravariance (in) with examples
Build a generic LRU cache in C# using Dictionary + LinkedList with unit tests

resources: C# Dictionary internals how it works

days.title: Caching Strategies
days.summary: Caching appears in nearly every design. Know the patterns, eviction policies and failure modes like stampede and stale data.

tasks.text: Learn cache-aside, read-through, write-through, write-behind and their consistency tradeoffs
Learn eviction (LRU/LFU/TTL), cache stampede, thundering herd and invalidation strategies
Learn CDN and edge caching, HTTP cache headers (Cache-Control, ETag)
Design on paper: add a Redis cache layer to a product catalog API with invalidation on update

resources: CDN how it works system design

days.title: React Fundamentals Refresher
days.summary: Next.js questions assume solid React. Refresh rendering, state, props and reconciliation before moving to the App Router.

tasks.text: Review JSX, components, props, state, one-way data flow and lifting state up
Learn reconciliation, virtual DOM, keys and why index keys cause bugs
Build a React + TypeScript todo app (Vite) with filters and controlled inputs
Write answers to: what triggers a re-render and how to prevent unnecessary ones

days.title: Stack Patterns
days.summary: Stacks solve matching, parsing and next-greater-element problems. The monotonic stack is a high-yield interview pattern.

tasks.text: LeetCode 20 - Valid Parentheses (Easy)
LeetCode 155 - Min Stack (Medium)
LeetCode 150 - Evaluate Reverse Polish Notation (Medium)
LeetCode 739 - Daily Temperatures (Medium) - monotonic stack

days.title: Indexing Deep Dive
days.summary: Index questions separate seniors from juniors. Know B-trees, clustered vs nonclustered, covering and composite index ordering.

tasks.text: Learn B-tree structure, clustered vs nonclustered, covering indexes with INCLUDE
Learn composite index column order, selectivity, and Postgres GIN/BRIN/partial indexes
Build: seed 1M rows in Postgres (Docker) and compare EXPLAIN ANALYZE before/after indexes
Write notes: when an index hurts (writes, low selectivity, functions on columns)

days.title: Week 2 Review
days.summary: Lock in sliding window and stack patterns and the caching vocabulary. Redo anything that felt shaky.

tasks.text: Re-solve LeetCode 3, 15 and 739 blind
Write a one-page cheat sheet on caching patterns and eviction
Explain clustered vs nonclustered indexes out loud in 90 seconds

days.title: Binary Search
days.summary: Binary search applies to sorted arrays and to answer spaces (search on the result). A single reliable template prevents off-by-one bugs.

tasks.text: LeetCode 704 - Binary Search (Easy) - memorize one template
LeetCode 74 - Search a 2D Matrix (Medium)
LeetCode 875 - Koko Eating Bananas (Medium) - binary search on answer
LeetCode 33 - Search in Rotated Sorted Array (Medium)

resources: search in rotated sorted array explanation

days.title: LINQ, Delegates and Lambdas
days.summary: LINQ is daily .NET work and interviewers test deferred execution and IQueryable translation. Delegates and events underpin LINQ and many frameworks.

tasks.text: Learn deferred vs immediate execution, multiple enumeration pitfalls, yield return
Learn Func/Action/Predicate, events, closures, and expression trees behind IQueryable
Solve 10 LINQ exercises: GroupBy, Join, SelectMany, Aggregate, Zip, ToLookup
Build a custom LINQ-style extension method WhereIf and a lazy Batch(n) iterator

days.title: Angular Components and Standalone
days.summary: Modern Angular is standalone-first with signals-based inputs and new control flow. Interviewers expect you to know both NgModules and the new model.

tasks.text: Learn standalone components vs NgModules, lifecycle hooks, content projection
Learn input()/output() signal APIs, model(), and @if/@for/@switch control flow
Build an Angular 17+ standalone app: product list with filter, child components, @for with track
Write notes: ngOnChanges vs ngOnInit vs ngAfterViewInit and when each fires

days.title: Load Balancing and Proxies
days.summary: Load balancers are in every diagram, so know L4 vs L7, algorithms and health checks. Consistent hashing returns in caching and sharding questions.

tasks.text: Learn L4 vs L7 load balancing, round robin, least connections, health checks, sticky sessions
Learn reverse proxy vs API gateway vs service mesh (NGINX, YARP, Envoy)
Learn consistent hashing with virtual nodes and where it is used
Design: highly available API tier with LB failover across two availability zones

days.title: Linked List I
days.summary: Linked list problems test pointer discipline. Draw nodes before coding and master fast/slow pointers.

tasks.text: LeetCode 206 - Reverse Linked List (Easy) - iterative and recursive
LeetCode 21 - Merge Two Sorted Lists (Easy)
LeetCode 141 - Linked List Cycle (Easy) - Floyd fast/slow
LeetCode 143 - Reorder List (Medium)

days.title: Docker Fundamentals
days.summary: Docker is assumed knowledge for senior backend roles. Understand images, layers and caching, not just docker run.

tasks.text: Learn images vs containers, layers and build cache, volumes, networks
Learn Dockerfile instructions: FROM, COPY, RUN, ENTRYPOINT vs CMD, ARG vs ENV
Build: Dockerize a .NET 8 Web API and run it with port mapping and env vars
Inspect layers with docker history and reorder Dockerfile to maximize cache hits

days.title: Week 3 Review
days.summary: Consolidate binary search, linked lists, LINQ and Docker. Rehearse explanations, not just code.

tasks.text: Re-solve LeetCode 33, 875 and 143 blind
Explain deferred execution and IQueryable vs IEnumerable out loud
Summarize LB algorithms and consistent hashing in a diagram
Update your mistake log with patterns you missed this week

resources: how to keep a leetcode mistake log

days.title: Linked List II and Tree Basics
days.summary: Finish key linked list mediums and begin trees with recursion. Recursive thinking on trees is the gateway to graphs and DP.

tasks.text: LeetCode 19 - Remove Nth Node From End of List (Medium)
LeetCode 2 - Add Two Numbers (Medium)
LeetCode 226 - Invert Binary Tree (Easy)
LeetCode 104 - Maximum Depth of Binary Tree (Easy) - recursive and BFS

days.title: Async/Await Deep Dive
days.summary: Async is the most common senior .NET topic: state machines, deadlocks, ConfigureAwait and ValueTask. Being able to explain what the compiler generates is a strong signal.

tasks.text: Learn the async state machine, SynchronizationContext, ConfigureAwait(false), thread pool
Learn Task vs ValueTask, .Result/.Wait deadlocks, async void, CancellationToken propagation
Build a parallel HTTP fetcher with Task.WhenAll, SemaphoreSlim throttling and cancellation
Learn System.Threading.Channels and Parallel.ForEachAsync; note when to use each

resources: async await state machine C# explained

days.title: React Hooks Deep Dive
days.summary: Hooks questions probe effects, dependencies and memoization. Stale closures and effect cleanup are common traps.

tasks.text: Learn useState, useEffect dependencies and cleanup, useRef, useReducer, useContext
Learn useMemo/useCallback/React.memo and when memoization is wasted
Build custom hooks useDebounce and useFetch with abort on unmount
Write an explanation of stale closures with a broken and fixed example

days.title: Database Scaling
days.summary: Scaling the data tier is the heart of most designs. Know replication, partitioning, sharding keys and back-of-envelope estimates.

tasks.text: Learn leader-follower and multi-leader replication, read replicas and replication lag
Learn partitioning vs sharding, shard key choice, hot partitions, resharding
Practice back-of-envelope estimation: QPS, storage and bandwidth for 10M DAU
Design: shard a 1B-row orders table and explain the query patterns it supports

resources: back of envelope estimation system design

days.title: Trees: DFS and BFS

tasks.text: LeetCode 543 - Diameter of Binary Tree (Easy)
LeetCode 110 - Balanced Binary Tree (Easy)
LeetCode 102 - Binary Tree Level Order Traversal (Medium)
LeetCode 199 - Binary Tree Right Side View (Medium)

days.title: Multi-stage Builds and Compose
days.summary: Small, secure images and reproducible local stacks are expected from seniors. Compose mirrors the dependencies of your microservices.

tasks.text: Build a multi-stage Dockerfile for .NET 8 with non-root user and chiseled runtime image
Build docker-compose with API + Postgres + Redis + RabbitMQ using healthchecks and depends_on
Add .dockerignore, env files and named volumes; compare image sizes before/after
Write notes: how to keep secrets out of images and build args

days.title: Week 4 Review
days.summary: Phase 1 checkpoint. Confirm you can solve easy/medium array, stack, list and tree problems and explain async and scaling.

tasks.text: Re-solve LeetCode 102, 543 and 19 blind
Explain async/await deadlocks and ConfigureAwait out loud in 2 minutes
Write a Phase 1 summary: strongest and weakest areas, adjust next phase focus

days.title: Trees: BST and Subtrees

LeetCode 98 - Validate Binary Search Tree (Medium)

days.title: Memory Management and GC
days.summary: Understanding the GC, generations and allocation-free APIs shows you can fix production performance issues. Expect questions on IDisposable and Span.

tasks.text: Learn stack vs heap, GC generations, LOH/POH, workstation vs server GC
Learn IDisposable, using, finalizers, Dispose pattern and IAsyncDisposable
Learn Span<T>, Memory<T>, stackalloc and ArrayPool; rewrite a string parser with Span
Use dotnet-counters and dotnet-gcdump to find a leak in an event-handler sample app

days.summary: Angular DI is hierarchical and very different from ASP.NET Core DI. Interviewers love asking where a service instance lives.

tasks.text: Learn hierarchical injectors, providedIn root, component-level providers, inject()
Learn InjectionToken, useFactory/useValue/useExisting and multi providers

days.title: Message Queues and Async Processing
days.summary: Queues decouple services and absorb spikes, but bring delivery semantics and ordering problems. Your RabbitMQ experience is a strength here.

tasks.text: Learn queue vs pub/sub, at-most/at-least/exactly-once, idempotent consumers, DLQ
Compare RabbitMQ exchanges/queues with Kafka partitions/consumer groups/offsets
Learn backpressure, ordering guarantees and poison message handling
Design an order processing pipeline with retries, DLQ and idempotency keys

days.title: Tries and Tree Construction
days.summary: Tries power prefix search and autocomplete. Tree construction and max path sum are classic hard-ish tree problems.

LeetCode 124 - Binary Tree Maximum Path Sum (Hard)

days.title: Transactions and Isolation Levels
days.summary: Isolation levels and concurrency anomalies come up whenever money or inventory is involved. Know how Postgres MVCC differs from SQL Server locking.

tasks.text: Learn ACID and read anomalies: dirty, non-repeatable, phantom reads, lost update, write skew
Learn isolation levels, Postgres MVCC vs SQL Server locking and RCSI/snapshot
Reproduce a lost update in two psql sessions, then fix with SELECT FOR UPDATE
Implement optimistic concurrency with rowversion/xmin in EF Core and handle conflicts

days.title: Week 5 Review
days.summary: Review trees, GC and isolation levels. These are high-frequency senior topics.

tasks.text: Re-solve LeetCode 98, 105 and 208 blind
Explain GC generations and Span<T> benefits out loud
Draw a table of isolation levels vs anomalies from memory

days.title: Heap and Priority Queue

LeetCode 1046 - Last Stone Weight (Easy)

days.summary: Hiring manager rounds decide level. Present yourself as a senior engineer who leads, not only codes.

tasks.text: Research 3 target companies: product, stack, values, engineering blog
Polish a 2-minute tell me about yourself pitch aimed at senior/lead roles
Run a 45-min mock answering 6 STAR questions with a timer
Tailor reverse questions for each target company

resources: tell me about yourself senior engineer
how to research a company before interview

days.title: Full Loop: .NET Live Build
days.summary: Many European companies use take-home or live build rounds. Practice shipping a clean small service quickly.

tasks.text: Timed 90 min: build a minimal API with EF Core, validation, error handling and tests
Add a Dockerfile and a README explaining design decisions and tradeoffs
Self-review the code as a senior reviewer and list 5 improvements

days.title: Weak-spot Patch: DSA
days.summary: Use your mistake log to target the weakest patterns. Focused repair is worth more than new problems now.

tasks.text: Pick the 2 weakest patterns from your mistake log and re-read their templates
Solve 2 new NeetCode 150 problems from the weakest pattern
Solve 2 new NeetCode 150 problems from the second weakest pattern
Re-solve the 3 most-failed problems from the log

days.title: Weak-spot Patch: System Design
days.summary: Fix the parts of your designs that interviewers pushed on. Depth in one component beats breadth everywhere.

tasks.text: Redo your weakest mock design from scratch in 40 minutes
Deep dive one weak component (DB choice, caching, queues or consistency) with notes
Drill 3 back-of-envelope estimations in under 5 minutes each
Update your system design cheat sheet

days.title: Week 19 Review
days.summary: Review full loop feedback and confirm improvements on weak spots.

tasks.text: Summarize feedback from all full loop mocks into one page
Re-solve 2 problems from this week's weak-spot list blind
Retell the project deep dive in 10 minutes

days.title: Final Timed Mock
days.summary: One last realistic coding session to confirm readiness. Stay calm and narrate your thinking.

tasks.text: Timed 25 min: LeetCode 128 - Longest Consecutive Sequence (Medium)
Timed 25 min: LeetCode 567 - Permutation in String (Medium)
Timed 35 min: one random Hard from NeetCode 150 you have not solved
Write final notes on your interview routine: clarify, examples, approach, code, test

days.title: Final Mock: Collaborative Editor
days.summary: Google Docs design tests real-time collaboration and conflict resolution. A final chance to practice structure and timing.

tasks.text: 45-min mock: design Google Docs real-time collaborative editing
Deep dive: OT vs CRDT, WebSocket sessions, presence and document storage/versioning
Review all previous designs and write the 5 patterns you reuse most

days.title: Final Polish: Stories and Negotiation
days.summary: Finalize stories and prepare for offers. European and remote offers vary in salary, contracts and benefits.

tasks.text: Polish your top 8 STAR stories into a single printable page
Research senior salary bands for target countries/remote on levels.fyi and Glassdoor
Learn contract types (employment, EOR, B2B), relocation and notice period questions
Write and rehearse a negotiation script for salary expectations and counteroffers

resources: employer of record remote contract explained

days.title: Final Cheat Sheets
days.summary: Condense everything into cheat sheets you can skim before interviews. Writing them is itself a final review.

tasks.text: Write a one-page .NET cheat sheet: async, GC, DI, EF Core, ASP.NET Core, testing
Write a one-page database and DevOps cheat sheet: indexes, isolation, Redis, K8s, CI/CD
Skim the Angular and Next.js cheat sheets and fix any gaps

days.title: Light Practice: Confidence Set
days.summary: Keep skills warm without burning out. Solve problems you know well to build confidence.

tasks.text: Re-solve 5 favorite problems from different patterns in under 15 minutes each
Pattern flash drill: read 20 problem titles and name the pattern in 10 seconds each
Review your interview routine notes and complexity cheat sheet

days.title: Interview Logistics and Setup
days.summary: Remove avoidable stress. Test your setup and prepare everything you need for interview day.

tasks.text: Test camera, mic, lighting, internet and screen sharing; close notifications
Practice in CoderPad, HackerRank and an online whiteboard (Excalidraw/Miro)
Prepare interview day kit: resume, story sheet, reverse questions, water, schedule

days.title: Rest Day Before Interview
days.summary: Rest is part of preparation. A rested brain performs far better than one cramming the night before.

tasks.text: Skim your story sheet and cheat sheets for 20 minutes, then stop studying
Take a walk, exercise lightly and sleep at least 8 hours

resources: how to relax before a job interview
